title: Rural Queenslanders have seen gas projects come and go – but a 725-hectare datacentre poses a whole new level of ‘stupidity’
key_facts: A proposed $31 billion data centre on a 725-hectare feedlot site near Kogan, outside Dalby, Queensland, would power Anthropic's Claude model, the Guardian says.
Developer is Singapore-based Zerra DC; peak power 2.16 GW, about a quarter of total state demand; about 1,400 long-term jobs, according to the company.
Zerra says cooling water demand would be about that of an average shopping centre.
A local petition has over 21,500 signatures.
The Environmental Defenders Office reports a 250% rise in datacentre queries since January and calls for a moratorium.
On Friday the Queensland government said it would take over assessing data centre applications from local councils.
Premier David Crisafulli sees jobs and lower power bills; the Dalby mayor does not endorse or oppose the project.
quote_evidence: Last month came the biggest scheme yet, a $31bn datacentre to power Claude, the large language model developed by global AI giant Anthropic.
The state government will become the responsible assessor and coordinator of any data centre applications, instead of local councils”.
why_it_matters_hint: An Anthropic-linked mega-project triggers local resistance and a shift of approval power to the state.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (state announcement); project announced in Sep 2026
notes: Feature article. Planning-minister statement is quoted from a spokesperson.
